title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors and employees
tiers.description: All Directors and employees of the Company, undifferentiated; the policy applies the same insider trading, closed period, notification and Board veto rules to both groups with no separate regime for executives or a defined 'restricted persons' class.

windows.start_anchor: release of the quarterly report, half yearly results, preliminary annual results or lodgement of the Company's Annual Report
end of the financial year or half financial year
windows.end_anchor: release of the annual or half year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may veto an individual transaction notified to it outside the recommended four-week trading window; the policy does not say whether a veto or its reasons are kept confidential.

rules.section: Policy for trading in the Company's securities
rules.detail: The general insider trading prohibition is expressly extended to 'all division 3 financial products as defined by section 1042A', which includes derivatives, but only while the person holds price sensitive information not generally available to the market. There is no separate closed-period or general rule naming derivatives, and no defined 'Dealing' term extending clearance or notification duties to them.
rules.evidence: As a general rule Directors and employees of the Company must not buy or sell securities in the Company including trading in all division 3 financial products as defined by section 1042A of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) ... when they are in possession of price sensitive information which is not generally available to the market.

rules.detail: No mention of hedging, economic risk limitation, or equity incentive scheme securities anywhere in the policy.
Prepaid forwards, collars, or other monetisation structures are not referenced.
Short selling is not named; only 'short-term trading' (holding-period conduct) is addressed, which is a distinct concept.

rules.section: Policy for trading in the Company's securities
rules.detail: CFDs are not named, but as financial products they would fall within 'division 3 financial products' swept into the insider trading prohibition while the holder possesses price sensitive information; there is no independent CFD rule.
rules.evidence: must not buy or sell securities in the Company including trading in all division 3 financial products as defined by section 1042A of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) ... when they are in possession of price sensitive information

rules.detail: Margin lending, secured financing, and use of Company securities as collateral are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting a charge, lien, mortgage or other security interest over Company securities is not addressed.
No secured financing rule of any kind; the policy is limited to insider trading, short-term trading, closed periods and Chairman notification.

rules.section: Policy for trading in the Company's securities
rules.detail: Blanket ban on short-term trading, undefined by any holding period, LIFO basis, or carve-out.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading of any of the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman (standing notification before any dealing); Board (prior notice and veto power for transactions outside the recommended four-week window); Company Secretary (enquiry as to pending price sensitive announcements before trading even within the recommended window)
clearance.section: Policy for trading in the Company's securities
clearance.evidence: Directors and employees who wish to buy or sell securities in the Company are required to notify the Chairman prior to dealing in such securities. ... At all other times the Board must receive prior notice of transactions, which are subject to Board veto.

short_term.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading of any of the Company's securities.

exemption_authority: None stated; the closed period trading prohibition is expressed as absolute with no hardship or discretionary exception referenced.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or securities of a company in a "special relationship" with the Company when they are in possession of price sensitive information which is not generally available to the market
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The insider-trading-based restriction (and its division 3 financial products sweep) also reaches securities of, and by extension derivatives over, companies in a defined special relationship with Kingsgate, which is broader than the Company's own stock alone.

bespoke_clauses.clause: At all other times the Board must receive prior notice of transactions, which are subject to Board veto.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering, unwinding, or settling a collar outside the recommended four-week post-results window requires prior notice to the Board and can be blocked outright, with no stated process, timeframe, or right of review.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no secured financing or hedging regime
bespoke_clauses.clause: Policy for trading in the Company's securities [contains no reference to margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, or hedging]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This 2010-era policy predates any restriction on collateralising or hedging Company securities, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself prohibited by this document, though the derivative legs remain subject to the insider trading and closed period rules and general notification to the Chairman.

bespoke_clauses.clause: [No reference anywhere to unvested, vested, restricted, or equity incentive scheme securities]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy does not distinguish vested from unvested holdings, so it provides no separate gating for a collar over vested shares versus other holdings; general rules apply uniformly to all securities held.

summary: A funded collar appears possible under this policy, which is unusually thin: it contains no rule at all on margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, or hedging, so the loan secured on the collared shares is not addressed or prohibited. The purchased put and written call would be caught only by the general insider trading prohibition, which expressly extends to 'division 3 financial products' (including derivatives) while the director or employee possesses undisclosed price sensitive information, and by the absolute closed period ban between financial year end and results release. Outside those constraints, any dealing requires standing notification to the Chairman, and if executed outside the Company's recommended four-week post-results trading window, prior notice to the Board which retains an unqualified veto. There is no clearance system, no defined validity period, no minimum shareholding requirement, and no distinction between vested and unvested securities. Given the policy's age (2010) and narrow scope, a funded collar is best timed within the four-week post-results window, confirmed with the Company Secretary as free of pending price sensitive announcements, and notified to the Chairman in advance.
